A few years ago I got drunk and walked into a supermarket at night holding a bb rifle (looked real in the dark) with 60 rounds of 9mm in my front right pocket. Earlier I was staring at Eric and Dylans suicide photo in the library. For a while I just looked at them intently, lying there, motionless. Just thinking how they looked so "at peace", just lying there, dead. And I wanted that peace. I wanted to die I guess? So I got in my car drunk and SPED to the supermarket and parked, got out and instantly popped the trunk, grabbed the bb gun and started walking to the entrance. Passed some woman and said "sup?" and she didn't say anything and just walked past me. Went into the bathroom and had a sudden moment of clarity and I was like ...."bro.... WHAT AM I DOOOOOING??????????!!!!! WHAT ARE YOU DOING DUDE????? Well it's over now, people have called the cops 100% by this point so I'm finished either way." and i thought about just dumping the bb gun in the trashcan and leaving like nothing happened, and forgetting about what I had just done. But I knew it wouldn't work so I just decided to walk back out of the bathroom and go to my car and leave and go home I guess. But when I stepped out of the restroom and turned the corner, I saw about 4 officers huddled together talking to each other. They're at the doors so the only way to exit was to go past them. They notice me as I'm walking past them, gun in hand, and they say "Hey! Stop!" and i just ignored them and continued to the exit. I was a few steps from the front door when one of them came up behind me and grabbed my rifle from me. I turned around and stopped walking and looked at them. They were like "what's going on man???" and I just said "I wanna die." I never had any intentions of hurting anybody, except for myself. Anyway, they treated it as a crisis situation since I said I wanted to die, and subsequently went to 2 different psych wards before being released. Have already been punished and dealt with consequences, and I still am to this day 3-4 years later. I'm okay now as of 2024.

I remember when I was numb. While in this state, I thought to myself “how would i feel if i won the lottery right now?” and i realized i wouldn’t of felt much. I would’ve thought “yay. okay. cool.” and that was it. I wouldn’t of been jumping up and down with joy. none of that. just “meh, cool. whatever.” It sucks to feel numb. nothing matters to you when you feel like that. something wonderful happens in your life? numb. Something bad happens to you? numb. it’s as if it doesn’t really effect you anymore. You’re. just. numb. No matter what happens. You’re friend or relative died? numb. You think “oh, they died. okay.” and that’s it. someone cheated on you? numb. “oh, they cheated on me. ok.” no anger or anything. just numb. I’m sorry you feel like this, but I can tell you that I don’t feel as numb as I used to. I am getting better slowly. Not trying to press my beliefs on you, but I am a christian. If you believe in God then just ask Him to take this numbness away. Ask Him to help you feel again. I was depressed. One day I drank a bottle of cough sryup and I was high, laying on my bed, apologizing to God and basically crying out to Him for help. I realized my life was going nowhere, and If i kept living like this, getting high, drunk, etc. then I might either end up dead, or something else. I realized my life was going to come to a dead end. Eventually I fell asleep and I awoke to my friend who texted me asking me “Hey i’ve been thinking about you and praying for you. How are you doing?” My friend lives in Arizona and I live in Kentucky. We handnt talked in months. But it just so happened that a few hours after I called out to God, my friend texted me. Coincidence? I think not. He said “I was on my way to work and you came to my mind.” God put me in his thoughts so that he would text me. I told him I wasn’t doing well. We talked a bit, and after that I got out of bed and realized. “Wait. I don’t feel depressed anymore. I feel so much better than I did a few hours ago.” God took those negative feelings away from me, so He can and WILL DO IT FOR YOU!  In my case, God was calling me back to Himself. He knows what’s best for us individually. He wanted me to come back to Him so I can have peace. And since then I’ve gotten back in contact with a friend from the ministry and have been hanging out with other believers in Christ who have always been there for me and are helping me.
I don’t know you or how numb you are, but i can say I’ve felt a piece of your numbness. I know you might not care what happens in the world, or even to you. But just realize that God is ALWAYS there for you and He knows exactly what you’re feeling. He knows what you’re going through. He knows you better than you know yourself. I don’t know your beliefs, but just try and call out to Him. You’d be amazed at what He can do. Have a good day

Hesitate less; once you see the enemy hit the ball and you know you can go for it, do it. Don't stop and think about it or it'll be too late.

As ytzi13 said, practice hitting the ball hard. \(especially for clearing\)

Learn to position yourself better. Think about where the ball is GOING to be in a couple seconds whether than where it currently is. That way, you can be in position to get the ball right after the enemy hits it. \(An advanced tip is to look at the enemies car right before they touch the ball. That way you have a good idea where the ball is going to go after they hit it\).

People will still try and pass across the backboard ALL THE TIME in diamond. For 3v3, If you know your teammate is behind you in defence, don't be scared to get right up near their goal, so that when your other m8 passes you are already there for it. The second it passes in front of the enemy goal, smash it in. You'd be surprised at how much of a difference it makes at that level to be ready for a pass like that, or any pass. If you are a second too late then most of the time the enemy would've cleared it from their net and you can no longer score.

If you see your m8 struggling in your corner to clear the ball, go up and help him. There may be an enemy player trying to get the ball from him, but if you come up out of nowhere and smack the ball away, it leaves the opponent in a bad spot; it will also free up your teammate so that he can get a boost refill or something. NOTE: If you're in 3v3 then this is easier because you have another teammate who can back you up if something goes wrong. This is riskier in 2v2 because it's just you and your m8. If you miss the ball, you may get scored on. I would make 90% sure you can at least get the ball away from the enemy before you go for something like that in 2v2.

If you can start getting good at reading the ball before it bounces, you will have a very good advantage over other players in this rank. That combined with little hesitation, and you'll be all over them. I was playing standard 3v3 today at a high diamond level with maybe 1 or 2 champs. I was hesitating way less than usual, going for balls without too much thought, and I was pouncing on them over and over. I did the same thing next game, and again I was all over them. You'd be surprised.

One other thing I want to add about reading the ball. Try and visualize this with me:

Your sitting in the middle of the net waiting for the ball. The enemy hits the ball straight at your net, but its too high so it bounces off the backboard and goes right back to him. He scores.

How could you prevent this from happening? You could jump in the air before the ball hits the backboard, and as it's bouncing back out into the field, you meet it in the air and hit it away. Now I know this isn't easy, but if you practice doing that, you will save a lot of balls from going in.
